business_model.claim: Central Garden & Pet Company generates revenue by manufacturing and distributing branded and private label pet and lawn-and-garden products, and distributing third-party brands, across two reportable segments: Pet and Garden.
quotes: We operate through two reportable segments: Pet and Garden.

We produce both branded and private label products for our customers as well as distribute third-party brands that give our retail partners a breadth of selection from ultra-premium to value offerings.

business_model.claim: The Pet segment sells dog and cat supplies, aquatics, small animal, reptile, and pet bird supplies, equine and livestock products, animal health and insect control items, live fish and small animals, and outdoor cushions.
quotes: Our Pet segment offers a broad range of products for dog and cat supplies, including treats and chews, toys, beds and containment, grooming items, waste management and training pads.
This segment also includes live fish and small animals as well as outdoor cushions.

business_model.claim: The Garden segment sells lawn and garden consumables including grass seed, packet seed, wild bird feed and accessories, herbicides, insecticides, pesticides, fertilizers, and live plants.
quotes: Our Garden segment includes lawn and garden consumables such as grass seed; vegetable, flower and herb packet seed; wild bird feed, bird houses and other birding accessories; weed, grass, and other herbicides, insecticide and pesticide products; fertilizers and live plants.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025, consolidated net sales were $3.1 billion ($1.8 billion in Pet and $1.3 billion in Garden) and operating income was $250 million ($216 million in Pet, $142 million in Garden, and $108 million of corporate expenses).
quotes: In fiscal 2025, our consolidated net sales were $3.1 billion, of which our Pet segment, or Pet, accounted for approximately $1.8 billion and our Garden segment, or Garden, accounted for approximately $1.3 billion.

In fiscal 2025, our operating income was $250 million, consisting of income from our Pet segment of $216 million, income from our Garden segment of $142 million and corporate expenses of $108 million.

business_model.claim: In preliminary fiscal 2026 results, consolidated net sales fell 6% to $2.9 billion (Pet sales fell 11% to $1.6 billion and Garden sales increased 1% to $1.3 billion), while organic net sales grew 1% and operating income rose 14% to $286 million.
quotes: Net sales decreased 6% to $2.9 billion, due to the exit of the pet distribution business at the beginning of the third quarter, while organic net sales increased 1%.
Pet segment sales decreased 11% to $1.6 billion, while Pet organic sales increased 1%, led by growth in Professional and Dog Treats.
Garden segment sales increased 1% to $1.3 billion, with growth in Fertilizer, Wild Bird, and Grass Seed.
Operating income increased 14% to $286 million, with operating margin expanding 170 basis points to 9.7%.

business_model.claim: Branded products (Central brands and third-party brands produced by Central) accounted for approximately 79% of fiscal 2025 net sales, while other manufacturers' products accounted for 21%.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, sales of branded products represented approximately 79% of our net sales, compared to 78% in fiscal 2024, and sales of other manufacturers' products represented 21% of our net sales.

business_model.claim: In April 2026, Central exited its lower-margin pet distribution business ($474 million in fiscal 2025 net sales) by contributing approximately $57 million of net assets into a partnership with Phillips Pet Food & Supplies for $31 million in cash, a $5 million note receivable, and a 20% stake valued at $26 million.
quotes: Under the terms of the agreement, we contributed our pet distribution business, comprised of net assets of approximately $57 million, including inventory of approximately $69 million, into the newly formed entity.
We received cash proceeds of approximately $31 million, a note receivable of approximately $5 million and a 20% ownership interest in the newly formed partnership valued at $26 million.
Pet Distribution's net sales in fiscal 2025 were $474 million.

At the same time, gross margin improved due primarily to both the positive impact of the divestiture of our pet distribution business, which had lower margins, and our cost and simplicity initiatives in both segments.

business_model.claim: Central sells across national, regional, and independent brick-and-mortar retailers—including mass merchants, home improvement chains, pet specialty chains, farm and feed outlets, and roughly 5,900 independent pet stores—as well as online retailers.
quotes: We have long-standing relationships with leading national, regional and independent retailers across brick-and-mortar and online channels.

The retail channel is equally diverse, ranging from national chains like Petco, Pet Supplies Plus and PetSmart with over 6,000 locations to the roughly 5,900 independent stores, along with mass merchants, farm & feed outlets, and online retailers, including pet-centric e-tailers like Chewy with unlimited shelf space.

business_model.claim: Revenue is heavily concentrated in major retail accounts: Walmart (17% of fiscal 2025 net sales), Home Depot (16%), Costco, Lowe's, and Amazon together represented approximately 54% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and 2024.
quotes: Walmart, our largest customer, accounted for approximately 17% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 16% in fiscal 2024.
Home Depot, our second largest customer, represented approximately 16% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 17% in fiscal 2024.
Together with Costco, Lowe's and Amazon these major retailers represented approximately 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 2024.

business_model.claim: Central manufactures most of its branded products in U.S. facilities, supplemented by plants in Canada and Mexico and contract manufacturing, and operates an integrated logistics network that consolidates owned and third-party goods into single shipments.
quotes: We manufacture the majority of our branded products in our U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by select contract manufacturing arrangements, including an exclusive supply of our registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene.
Our integrated logistics system also consolidates products from other manufacturers with our branded products into single shipments.

business_model.claim: Garden revenue and profits are highly seasonal and weather-dependent: in fiscal 2025, 64% of Garden net sales and 57% of total net sales occurred in the second and third fiscal quarters, when substantially all Garden operating income is earned.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of our Garden segment’s net sales and 57% of our total net sales occurred during our second and third fiscal quarters.
Substantially all of the Garden segment’s operating income is generated in this period.

Because demand for lawn and garden products is significantly influenced by weather, particularly weekend weather during the peak gardening season, our results of operations and cash flow could also be adversely affected by certain weather patterns such as unseasonably cool or warm temperatures, heavy rains, water shortages or floods.

business_model.claim: Central's Cost and Simplicity agenda lowers manufacturing, logistics, and administrative costs through facility consolidations and SKU rationalization, helping expand fiscal 2026 GAAP gross margin by 240 basis points to 34.3% and cut SG&A by 3% to $724 million despite $24 million in closure and exit expenses.
quotes: Gross profit increased 1% to $1.0 billion, with gross margin expanding 240 basis points to 34.3%.
SG&A was $724 million, a reduction of 3%.

Central recognized incremental operating expense of $24 million, of which $14 million was recognized in its Pet segment, primarily related to the exit of a minor business and the closure of two facilities, and $10 million in its Garden segment related to remaining cost associated with the closure of five distribution centers in fiscal 2025 and 2024.

quotes: In particular, our Pennington and Kaytee businesses are exposed to fluctuations in market prices for commodity seeds and grains used to produce bird feed and grass seed.
As a result of this decline, in fiscal 2024, we incurred an approximately $15-$20 million charge to write-down the value of our grass seed inventory.

quotes: In fiscal 2025, less than 15% of our cost of goods sold was from products or materials sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.

Offsetting these charges, Central recognized incremental gross profit of $24 million for tariff refunds received, of which $22 million was recognized in its Pet segment and $2 million in its Garden segment.

quotes: To date, we have reduced the number of ERP systems from 46 to 6.

Corporate expenses increased $7.0 million due primarily to higher third-party provider expense, driven by M&A activity expenditures and higher payroll costs related to our investment in data improvement and AI readiness.

competitive_position.claim: Central holds leading positions in the U.S. pet supplies and lawn and garden consumables markets, competing in approximately $40 billion of a $158 billion U.S. pet market populated by more than 2,500 manufacturers.
quotes: We are a leader in both the U.S. pet supplies market and the lawn and garden consumables market.

Packaged Facts estimated that in 2025, U.S. retail sales of pet food, treats and chews, supplies, veterinary and non-medical services and live animals will total approximately $158 billion, with about $40 billion attributable to the categories where we compete.
According to Packaged Facts, the U.S. pet supplies market is highly fragmented, with more than 2,500 manufacturers, most operating in single or limited categories.

competitive_position.claim: Central owns a diversified portfolio of pet and garden brands—most marketed for over 40 years—with branded products accounting for approximately 79% of net sales in fiscal 2025, up from 78% in fiscal 2024.
quotes: The majority of our brands have been marketed for over 40 years, establishing deep consumer trust and strong market positions.
In fiscal 2025, sales of branded products represented approximately 79% of our net sales, compared to 78% in fiscal 2024, and sales of other manufacturers' products represented 21% of our net sales.

competitive_position.claim: Central manufactures the majority of its branded products in U.S.-based facilities with an exclusive supply arrangement for its registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene, and its Segrest subsidiary is the largest U.S. supplier of aquarium fish.
quotes: We manufacture the majority of our branded products in our U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by select contract manufacturing arrangements, including an exclusive supply of our registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene.
Our Segrest subsidiary is the largest supplier of aquarium fish in the United States and also supplies pet birds and small animals.

competitive_position.claim: Central operates one of the largest sales and distribution networks in the pet industry, consolidating products from other manufacturers with its own branded products into single shipments for mass-market, omnichannel, online, and independent retailers.
quotes: Our Pet segment is supported by one of the largest sales and distribution networks in the industry, which provides strategic reach and scale for our brands.
Our integrated logistics system also consolidates products from other manufacturers with our branded products into single shipments.
Many smaller players lack in-house sales and logistics capabilities and rely on distributors such as us to reach regional pet specialty chains and independent retailers.

competitive_position.claim: Central is one of the largest pet supplies vendors to Costco, Amazon, and Walmart, a leading supplier to independent U.S. pet retailers, among the largest lawn and garden consumables vendors to The Home Depot, Walmart, and Lowe’s, and Lowe’s fiscal 2025 Vendor Partner of the Year for Lawn & Garden.
quotes: We believe these strengths have positioned us as one of the largest pet supplies vendors to Costco, Amazon and Walmart, a leading supplier to independent pet retailers in the United States and among the largest lawn and garden consumables vendors to The Home Depot, Walmart and Lowe’s.
In fiscal 2025, Central was recognized as Lowe’s “Vendor Partner of the Year” for the Lawn & Garden division, reflecting the strength of our customer partnerships.

competitive_position.claim: Central faces intense competition in consolidating industries from national, regional, and private-label suppliers, including larger rivals with substantially greater revenue and resources such as Spectrum Brands, Mars, Inc., J.M Smucker Co., Scotts Miracle-Gro, and S.C. Johnson.
quotes: We operate in highly competitive industries, which have experienced increased consolidation in recent years.
We compete against numerous other companies, some of which are more established in their industries and have substantially greater revenue and resources than we do.

Our largest competitors in the Pet segment are Spectrum Brands, Mars, Inc. and the J.M Smucker Co., and our largest competitors in the Garden segment are Scotts Miracle-Gro, Spectrum Brands and S.C. Johnson.

competitive_position.claim: Central depends heavily on a small group of retailers, with Walmart (17%), Home Depot (16%), Costco, Lowe's, and Amazon together accounting for approximately 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Walmart, our largest customer in fiscal 2025, represented approximately 17% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 16% of total net sales in fiscal 2024 and 2023.
Home Depot, our second largest customer in fiscal 2025, represented approximately 16% of total net sales in fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023.
Costco, Lowe's and Amazon are also significant customers, and together with Walmart and Home Depot, accounted for approximately 54% of our net sales in fiscal 2025 and 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Consolidating retail customers exert growing buying power to resist price increases, shift to just-in-time destocking, and expand private-label shelf space, while third-party vendors can bypass Central's distribution to sell directly to retailers.
quotes: Our retailer customers have continued to consolidate, resulting in fewer customers on which we depend for business.
Consequently, our customers have been implementing inventory destocking and making purchases on a “just-in-time” basis.

While we view private label as an opportunity and supply many private label products to retailers, we could lose sales if key retailers replace our branded products with private label product manufactured by others.

Net sales in the Garden segment decreased 7% to $232 million, due to unfavorable weather for Live Plants, and lower sales in Central's distribution business resulting from a vendor's decision to sell directly to retailers.

competitive_position.claim: Rapid growth in pure-play eCommerce threatens Central's sales if traditional brick-and-mortar and independent pet specialty retail partners lose share or experience credit distress.
quotes: Pure-play eCommerce players continue to gain share, as younger, digitally-native consumers, now entering prime pet-owning years, outspend older generations.
To the extent that the key retailers, including retailers in the pet specialty segment, on which we depend lose share to the eCommerce channel, we could lose sales.
potential credit risk associated with certain brick and mortar retailers in the pet specialty segment;

competitive_position.claim: U.S. import tariffs and input-cost inflation threaten Central's product competitiveness and margins, with less than 15% of fiscal 2025 cost of goods sold sourced outside the United States—primarily from China, Brazil, and Mexico—alongside volatile commodity grain and seed prices.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, less than 15% of our cost of goods sold was from products or materials sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.

To the extent the United States imposes new or additional tariffs on these or other countries where we or our suppliers source products, or if new or additional tariffs or trade restrictions are implemented by the United States or other countries in connection with a global trade war, the cost of our products manufactured in other countries and imported into the United States could increase significantly, which in turn could adversely affect the demand for these products and have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
In particular, our Pennington and Kaytee businesses are exposed to fluctuations in market prices for commodity seeds and grains used to produce bird feed and grass seed.

competitive_position.claim: Softening consumer discretionary spending, post-pandemic declines in durable pet goods demand, and shifting consumer preferences threaten organic sales growth, contributing to a 5% organic sales drop in the Pet segment in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
quotes: For example, in the last few years, we have seen a decline in demand for durable goods in certain of our categories, resulting in part from the residual effect of inflated demand for durable goods in the early years of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Net sales in the Pet segment decreased 29% to $305 million, while Pet organic net sales decreased 5%.

The decrease in organic net sales was due to softer consumer demand in certain categories, lost distribution in lower-margin pet beds and a temporary supply constraint in one of Central's pet businesses.

competitive_position.claim: Central's Garden segment is highly seasonal—generating approximately 64% of segment net sales and 57% of total net sales in the second and third fiscal quarters of fiscal 2025—making earnings highly vulnerable to adverse peak-season weather and long-term climate shifts.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of our Garden segment’s net sales and 57% of our total net sales occurred during our second and third fiscal quarters.
Unfavorable weather during the peak garden season in the future could have a significant adverse effect on the sales and profitability of our lawn and garden business.

Our failure to adequately manage the political, legal, regulatory, consumer and retail impacts of climate change could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

competitive_position.claim: Execution missteps in Central's Central to Home strategy, Cost and Simplicity restructuring, remaining ERP system consolidation from 46 to 6 systems, integration of Burpee and TRIXIE, and transition to the Phillips pet distribution partnership could raise costs or disrupt operations.
quotes: There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully execute our Central to Home strategic initiatives or that we will be able to do so within the anticipated time period.
To date, we have reduced the number of ERP systems from 46 to 6.
the impact of the new pet distribution partnership on our financial results and ability to distribute and promote our pet branded products;
risks associated with our expanded international operations following the TRIXIE acquisition, including compliance with foreign laws and regulations;

competitive_position.claim: Central also faces risks from slow consumer adoption of garden innovations, potential product recalls or liability claims, government restrictions or avian flu affecting live-animal and bird-feed demand, and environmental remediation liabilities at acquired facilities.
quotes: We believe that the period of time to gain consumer acceptance of major innovations is longer in the garden industry than in many industries, which compounds the risks generally associated with major new product innovations.

Product recalls or other governmental regulatory action directed at product sales could result in increased governmental scrutiny, reputational harm, reduced demand by consumers for our products, decreased willingness by retailer customers to purchase or provide marketing support for those products, unavailability or increased cost of insurance, or additional safety and testing requirements.
These restrictions have resulted in reduced availability of new pet birds and small animals and thus reduced demand for pet bird and small animal food and supplies.

With our extensive acquisition history, we have acquired a number of manufacturing and distribution facilities, and most of these facilities have not been subjected to Phase II environmental tests to determine whether they are contaminated.

The loss of, or significant adverse change in, our relationship with any of these key retailers could cause our net sales, operating income and cash flow to decline.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Q3 fiscal 2026 MD&A [P4] and fiscal 2026 earnings release [P6].
growth_thesis.claim: Central uses acquisitions to expand its brand portfolio and international reach, acquiring W. Atlee Burpee Company and agreeing to buy an 80% interest in TRIXIE for up to €400 million.

KG (“TRIXIE”), the leading European pet supplies and pet snacks company, for €340 million in cash at closing plus up to €60 million in additional earn-out payments, for total consideration of up to €400 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A [P2], Q3 fiscal 2026 MD&A [P4], and fiscal 2026 earnings release [P6].

quotes: The consummation of the Company’s acquisition of TRIXIE is subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions.
If the balance of the implementation is not executed successfully, we could experience business interruptions or material weaknesses relating to IT controls of acquired companies.
•risks associated with our expanded international operations following the TRIXIE acquisition, including compliance with foreign laws and regulations;

growth_thesis.claim: Central pursues organic growth and market share gains by developing differentiated new products and reinvesting cost savings into brand building and demand creation.
quotes: We are focusing on developing differentiated new products and reinvesting some of our annual cost savings into brand building and demand creation to deliver sustainable organic growth and expand market share.

Recent marketing initiatives, including our Farnam “Everything for the Ride”, Nylabone’s 70th birthday campaign and DoMyOwn’s “Chief Solutions Officer” initiative with Richard Karn have delivered promising results, accelerating growth and driving share gains across multiple brands.

growth_thesis.claim: For innovation-driven growth to continue, new products and improved formulations must achieve timely market acceptance and generate enough sales to recoup investments, despite slower adoption in gardening.
quotes: We cannot assure you that we will be successful in the introduction, marketing and production of any new products or product innovations, or that we will develop and introduce in a timely manner, improvements to our existing products which satisfy customer needs or achieve market acceptance.

We believe that the period of time to gain consumer acceptance of major innovations is longer in the garden industry than in many industries, which compounds the risks generally associated with major new product innovations.

growth_thesis.claim: Central is expanding its digital capabilities and optimizing its supply chain for high-demand online items to capture demand shifting toward eCommerce, omnichannel, and direct-to-consumer shopping.
quotes: Today's convenience-oriented consumers increasingly rely on eCommerce channels, including pure-play, omnichannel and direct-to-consumer, as part of their shopping routine.
To meet this demand, we continue to expand our digital and eCommerce capabilities while ensuring the right policies, products and programs enable all channels to compete effectively.
At the same time, we are optimizing our supply chain for high-demand eCommerce items, ensuring customer and consumer availability requirements are fulfilled at optimal cost.

growth_thesis.claim: For eCommerce expansion to drive net growth, Central's digital channel investments must succeed rapidly enough to offset potential sales losses at brick-and-mortar and pet specialty customers.
quotes: To the extent that the key retailers, including retailers in the pet specialty segment, on which we depend lose share to the eCommerce channel, we could lose sales.
We continue to make additional investments to access this channel more effectively, but there can be no assurances that any such investments will be successful.

growth_thesis.claim: Long-term Pet segment growth is supported by demographic shifts, pet humanization and premiumization, and heightened health and wellness focus, with younger owners spending more on pets.
quotes: We expect the U.S. pet supplies market to continue to grow, supported by long-term trends, including demographics shifts, humanization and premiumization of pets, and heightened focus on health and wellness.
Pet ownership is evenly split between younger generations (Gen Z and Millennials) and older generations (Gen X and Baby Boomers), with younger owners spending more on their pet.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A [P2] and Q4 fiscal 2026 results [P6].

quotes: If these restrictions become more severe, or similar restrictions become applicable to pet fish, our future sales of these products would likely suffer, which would negatively impact our profitability.
A significant outbreak in the United States would reduce demand for our pet and wild bird food and negatively impact our financial results.

growth_thesis.claim: Central grew fiscal 2026 GAAP operating income by 14% to $286 million and expanded non-GAAP gross margin to 33.6% through mix improvement, cost savings, and exiting the lower-margin pet distribution business.
quotes: Operating income increased 14% to $286 million, with operating margin expanding 170 basis points to 9.7%.

On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes tariff refunds received during the year, gross profit decreased 1% to $990 million, with gross margin expanding 150 basis points to 33.6%, driven by mix improvement and cost savings.

At the same time, gross margin improved due primarily to both the positive impact of the divestiture of our pet distribution business, which had lower margins, and our cost and simplicity initiatives in both segments.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors [P2] and fiscal 2027 outlook [P6].
growth_thesis.claim: For margin-driven earnings growth to continue, Central must execute its Cost and Simplicity agenda while offsetting tariff, energy, and commodity seed and grain cost pressures without losing sales volume.
quotes: There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully execute our Cost and Simplicity agenda or that we will be able to do so within the anticipated time period, which could adversely impact our ability to improve or maintain margins and enhance long-term profitability.

If we are unable to pass through higher input costs by raising the price of our products or altering our sourcing, we may experience organic sales declines and gross margin and operating income declines.
This outlook excludes the impact of any other acquisitions, divestitures or restructuring activities that may occur during fiscal 2027 and any further tariffs.

quotes: If cash on hand and borrowings under our credit facility are ever insufficient to meet our seasonal needs or if cash flow generated during the spring and summer is insufficient to repay our borrowings on a timely basis, this seasonality could have a material adverse effect on our business.

material_events.claim: Central entered into a definitive Purchase Agreement to acquire an 80% interest in TRIXIE Heimtierbedarf GmbH & Co. KG for approximately €340 million in cash at closing plus an earn-out of up to €60.0 million, for total consideration of up to €400 million.
quotes: On July 27, 2026, we announced we entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) to acquire 80% of the outstanding shares of TRIXIE Heimtierbedarf GmbH & Co. KG, a German limited partnership (“TRIXIE”) together with certain related entities.

Under the terms of the Purchase Agreement, the Company will pay a total consideration of up to €400 million, with an upfront consideration of approximately €340 million paid in cash at closing and an earn-out potential of up to €60.0 million based on 2026 performance, each subject to certain adjustments.
The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

material_events.claim: Central divested its pet distribution business (net assets of approximately $57 million) into a new partnership with Phillips Pet Food & Supplies in exchange for approximately $31 million in cash proceeds, an approximately $5 million note receivable, and a 20% partnership interest valued at $26 million, recognizing a pre-tax gain of $2.5 million.
quotes: On April 13, 2026, we entered into a strategic partnership with Phillips Pet Food & Supplies ("Phillips"), a leading national distributor of pet products, to form a new pet distribution business.

Under the terms of the agreement, we contributed our pet distribution business, comprised of net assets of approximately $57 million, including inventory of approximately $69 million, into the newly formed entity.
We received cash proceeds of approximately $31 million, a note receivable of approximately $5 million and a 20% ownership interest in the newly formed partnership valued at $26 million.
As a result of the transaction, we recognized a pre-tax gain of $2.5 million during the quarter ended June 27, 2026, which is included in Other income.

we have excluded the impact of tariff refunds and the associated interest received for certain tariffs previously imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act which were deemed unconstitutional.
